distributions.what: The STANDING BASELINE's per-window PnL, one value per walk-forward window — the OFF arm that a candidate grid is paired against. This is the object the campaign mean is a mean OF; the grid ruler needs the values, not the summary, because its instrument is a PAIRED per-window delta (V247_RULER.md §1: "A verdict is a paired per-window Δ (ON − OFF) aggregated per regime").
distributions.config: universe_selective (V227-skew + universe_selective_enabled, V240.A ADOPTED) — identical to the `config` field above. This IS the standing main arm.
distributions.corroboration: The same 32 OFF-arm values appear byte-identically (max abs diff 0.000) in FOUR other committed grids on the same volume — v240_wf, v241, v243a_wf and v245 — which is the cross-check scripts/v247_ruler.py performs at startup. Their per-regime means reproduce the journal to the cent: crisis +$598.53, trend +$2,996.92, recent +$29.64 (README.md:36-38 rounds these to +$599 / +$2,997 / +$30). All 32 cells carry determinism PASS with pnl_spread $0.00.
distributions.windows_manifest: data/walk_forward_manifest.json — every window id below is a windows[].id there, and every regime below equals that entry's windows[].regime (verified at transcription).

grid_ruler.spec: omega/nodes/victoria/training_log/V247_RULER.md (Phase 0, the instrument) and V247_RULER_CANDIDATES.md (Phase 1, candidate β = PRIMARY, adopted). Implemented by omega/eval/grid_ruler.py.
grid_ruler.instrument: paired per-window Δ (candidate − standing baseline), aggregated per regime family and pooled. V247_RULER.md §1: "A verdict is a paired per-window Δ (ON − OFF) aggregated per regime" — and, of the two distributions named there, only the paired Δ is the verdict instrument; the OFF-arm LEVEL spread "can never be the gate".
grid_ruler.bar: one-sided NO-REGRESSION. A family FAILS iff its mean-Δ is more negative than that family's MDE. V247_RULER.md §7 states the thresholds as a symmetric unfalsifiability rule ("claims below $X at n=Y: unfalsifiable, may not be used as an acceptance bar"); §6 names the direction this module gates in — "a floor does not need to DETECT small effects, only to reject large regressions".
grid_ruler.mde_formula: MDE = (z_{1-α/2} + z_{power}) · sd / sqrt(n) = 2.801585 · sd / sqrt(n), two-sided α=0.05 at 80% power (V247_RULER.md §4, and scripts/v247_ruler.py:mde). Normal approximation — slightly optimistic below n≈15, as the doc says. The ruler recomputes it at the grid's ACTUAL n so a short grid gets a correspondingly WIDER bar rather than the published one applied out of range.

delta_sd_usd._what: Δ-sd per family per COUPLING CLASS. V247_RULER.md §3 finding 1: "Δ-sd is mechanism-conditional, by up to 5×"; §7: "Any pre-reg must declare its expected coupling class — it determines which MDE row applies." Rows transcribed from §3's table (per-grid) and §4's table (median).

median._cite: V247_RULER.md §4, "median Δ sd" column — the mechanism-AGNOSTIC row, and the one §7's standing thresholds are computed from

inert._cite: V247_RULER.md §3, v245_gdelt row — "a V245-class near-inert feed"

low._cite: V247_RULER.md §3, v246_exit_adapt row — "a V246-class low-coupling mechanism" (exit-only / sizing-only)

heavy._cite: V247_RULER.md §3, v241_reasoning row — "a V241-class heavy intervention" (selection-changing). §4: "heavy-coupling mechanisms are unmeasurable on this manifest, full stop."

grid_ruler.why_default_median: A coupling class is a PRE-REGISTRATION act (V247_RULER.md §7), not something a scorer may infer from results. Absent a declared class the ruler uses the mechanism-agnostic median row, which is exactly the row §7's standing thresholds are stated in ($1,043 recent / $4,118 trend / $1,565 crisis at current n). It is also the CONSERVATIVE choice for a no-regression gate on a low-coupling bet: median Δ-sd exceeds the low-coupling Δ-sd in every family, so the bar is wider and the ruler is SLOWER to shout FAIL than a class-specific bar would be. Declaring `--coupling low` narrows it.

published_mde_usd_at_current_n._cite: V247_RULER.md §4 / §7 — recomputing the formula above at n = 10/10/12/32 reproduces these to within $1 (the residual is the doc's own inconsistent rounding: recent computes to 1,043.64 and is published as 1,043; pooled computes to 1,424.35 and is published as 1,425). tests/test_grid_ruler.py pins all four.

grid_ruler.advisory_recent_floor_note: Candidate β's "recent no-regression floor (one-sided): recent mean-Δ ≥ −1·SE (≈ −$360 for low-coupling mechanisms)" (V247_RULER_CANDIDATES.md §β). REPORTED, NOT GATED here — β says exact $ bars "are fixed in the pre-reg BEFORE any run", so a standing scorer may not impose one it invented. A pre-registration that adopts it turns it into a failure by setting gate_advisory_recent_floor true.
grid_ruler.dual_tail: β's third clause: "report BOTH Δ-p25 and level-p25 per regime; the pre-reg must name which one it gates on." Both are reported per family. Neither is gated — same reason as the recent floor.

bootstrap._cite: matches scripts/v247_ruler.py (BOOT_N=20000, random.Random(42)) so a ruler CI is comparable with the published §2/§3 CIs

notes: WHY per_cell_floor_usd AND campaign_mean_usd ARE TWO DIFFERENT NUMBERS (2026-08-19). campaign_mean_usd (+$599 / +$2,997 / +$30) is the MEAN of a per-regime walk-forward DISTRIBUTION (crisis n=12, trend n=10, recent n=10 x 90-day windows, README.md:27-38), not the PnL of any single cell — and those distributions are heavily right-skewed: crisis's own MEDIAN is +$65 against a +$599 mean, and recent's median is -$644 against a +$30 mean. Applying a family mean as a per-cell bar would therefore FAIL the majority of legitimate cells (over half of crisis, and most of recent, by construction) — an alarm that cries wolf until nobody reads it. So the campaign mean is NOT a per-cell bar, and is not used as one.

per_cell_floor_usd IS the unambiguous per-cell bar: a cell that LOSES MONEY fails, and nothing else does. 0.0 for all three families. It is a floor a legitimate cell can be judged against without knowing the shape of the family distribution: PnL < 0 needs no distributional argument to be bad news. Configurable per family so a future pre-registration can raise a family's bar; raising it is a journal act, not a convenience.

campaign_mean_usd is retained as INFORMATIONAL. A cell whose PnL is >= its per-cell floor but < its family's campaign mean passes, and carries advisory="below_campaign_mean" with the margin. It never affects the verdict. The campaign mean is a GRID-level ruler (a mean over the whole per-regime window set), so the honest comparison against it is a whole-grid aggregation, which this module does not yet do — see V247_RULER.md for what that instrument has to look like (pooled paired-delta MDE ~$875 for a low-coupling mechanism; per-regime MDE $1,043 recent / $1,565 crisis / $4,118 trend).
The numbers are per-FAMILY, not per-version. Do not edit them to make a run pass. V271.md:82 lists the standing baseline under "Never" for files a version may touch.
trade_count_floor 20 is carried over verbatim from omega/eval/v49_gates.py (lowered 50 -> 20 on 2026-04-06 after a 100-cycle zero streak from low signal dispersion).

There is no drawdown floor here on purpose: scripts/run_training.py never writes observability.max_drawdown_usd, so the v49 drawdown_ceiling gate compared 0.0 <= 0.0 and was permanently, vacuously green. The standing gate reports drawdown_ceiling as not_evaluated until a run actually emits the number.
